Theme

Body, health & movement

operate verb

on a patient

also operate on, be operated on, have an operation

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.53: C. Marius … cum secārētur
Traupman 169, 354, 388: chīrurgus eam secuit, the surgeon operated on her

secō, secāre, secuī, sectum

verb, first conjugation

operate on (literally, cut)

To have an operation is to be cut: secārī. The surgeon is chīrurgus (Traupman 169; Greek χειρουργός).

Examples

  • C. Marius, rūsticānus vir, sed plānē vir, cum secārētur, ut suprā dīxī, prīncipiō vetuit sē alligārī

    Gaius Marius, a countryman but every inch a man, when he was being operated on, as I said above, at first refused to be tied downCic. Tusc. 2.53

  • nec quisquam ante Marium solūtus dīcitur esse sectus

    and no one before Marius is said to have been operated on without being tied downCic. Tusc. 2.53

See also operation, doctor, hospital.
